english.title: Harassment - put in fear of violence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) caused **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to fear that violence would be used against

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

by your course of conduct which you knew or ought to have known would cause fear of violence to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) on each occasion in that **(..DETAIL DATES, PLACES AND NATURE OF CONDUCT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4(1) and (4) of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
cause fear of violence

knew/ought to know
would cause fear of violence on each occasion

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The maximum penalty on indictment was increased from five to ten years from 3rd April 2017, this offence wording also applies where the conduct occurred over two or more days before and after that date, see section 175 of the Policing and Crime Act 2017. See H7/PH97002 for offences committed before that date. .
(ii) See section 4(5) for alternative verdict.
(iii) Harassing a person may include alarming or causing the person distress; a "course of conduct" must involve conduct on at least two occasions and "conduct" includes speech.
(iv) The conduct must have taken place on at least two occasions on or after 30th September 1998.
(v) Incidents in cases of harassment must be so connected in type and in context as to justify the conclusion that they amounted to a course of conduct. See R v Patel [2004] EWCA Crim 3284
(vi) See section 4B of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 regarding the committing of this offence by a UK national or a person habitually resident in England and Wales whilst wholly or partly in a country outside the UK.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
